events.text: 80 protocells introduced in 8 independent founder lineages.

Controlled tissue study: 80 single cells, including one supplied precursor with strong tissue potentials. Growth, feeding, transport, damage, repair and reproduction use ecosystem rules; no adult is introduced.
A daughter cell stayed attached. The first colony formed.
Local food, stress and neighboring signals changed cell functions through inherited regulatory rules.
A growing colony has inherited the potential for contractile tissue.
A colony expresses distinct cell functions.
Structural cells support a larger body plan.
A larger colony consumed a smaller organism's exposed cell. Digested energy can fund division; remaining material returns to the habitat.
A differentiated colony contracts physical links between cells.
A colony moves through contraction and repeated ground contacts. This is physical locomotion, not a walking unlock.
